problem:
The population of a bacterial culture $P(t)$ after $t$ hours can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=-P.
$$

If there are currently $30$ bacteria in the culture, calculate the population after $3$ hours. Round your answer to the nearest integer.

The population after $3$ hours is approximately 
{{field-1}}
bacteria.

feedback.problem:
The number of sales $S(t)$ of a new tech device $t$ weeks after the start of sales can be modeled by the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=-0.1S.
$$

If there were $100\,000$ sales initially, calculate the number of sales after $10$ weeks. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the number of sales using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=-0.1S.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
S(t)={S}_{0}\,{e}^{-0.1t},
$$

where ${S}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that there were $100\,000$  sales initially, so we have ${S}_{0}=100\,000.$

Therefore, the number of sales $S$ at time $t$ is

$$
S(t)=100\,000\,{e}^{-0.1t}\,.
$$

Finally, to find the number of sales when $t=10,$ we substitute $t=10$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S(10) & =100\,000\,{e}^{-0.1\cdot 10} \\  & =100\,000\,{e}^{-1} \\  & ≈36\,787.94\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that there are $36\,788$ sales after $10$ weeks.
